explain.title: Understanding If Statements
explain.content: This lesson builds practical skill in If Statements within the module 'Conditionals'. Students connect the concept to robotics scenarios, practice with code, and verify understanding through quick checks.
keyPoints: Connect concept to real robot behavior
Use readable, testable code patterns
Check expected behavior with simple validation
Prepare for the next lesson in the sequence

example.title: If Statements Example
example.code:
# If Statements
power_level = 75
is_ready = True

if is_ready:
    print(f"Robot power: {power_level}%")

explain.title: Project Brief: Safety Decision Engine
explain.content: This module-end project applies concepts from 'Conditionals' to a useful robot utility students can run, test, and iterate.
keyPoints: Build practical utility, not just syntax drills
Use clear variable names and modular logic
Validate expected output with test cases
Reflect on reliability improvements

example.title: Starter Utility Pattern
example.code:
# Safety Decision Engine
battery_level = 82
target_distance_cm = 35
path_clear = True

if path_clear and battery_level > 40:
    print(f"Run mission to {target_distance_cm}cm")
else:
    print("Hold and recheck")

annotations.note: Use boolean logic for go or hold decisions

exercise.title: Build and Demonstrate
exercise.instructions:
1. Build the full utility for this module topic.
2. Include at least one function and one validation check.
3. Run three test cases and log outputs.
4. Add one improvement for readability or reliability.
5. Submit code and short reflection.
